findings.title: Group view-member enumeration mixes resource ID and resource name
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(),...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource the resource name is the groupId (group.getId()) and the store ID is an internal UUID. hasPermission() then does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing getId() never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz resource UUIDs instead of group IDs. Consumers put this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS for user search/count filtering, so filtering by group membership is broken (wrong users visible / invisible). Use getName() for lookup and for the result set.

findings.title: Global canManage() granted by view-only group permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true for hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only view permission on all-groups therefore passes requireManage(), which gates GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (create top-level group). Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE. The global check must require only MANAGE, otherwise a view-only administrator can create groups (privilege escalation).

findings.title: Per-user resource shadows all-users permission
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission() looks up resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()); if found it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the Users type resource. When both a per-user resource and an all-users permission exist, the all-users grant is ignored. An admin with MANAGE/VIEW on all-users loses access to any user that has a per-user resource created for another admin, breaking the documented fallback to all-users/all-groups. The check must OR the specific resource evaluation with the type-resource evaluation. Same pattern exists in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission().

findings.title: Possible NPE when all-groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) without null-checking resource. getResourceTypeResource() returns null when the schema is unsupported or init has not created the type resource. Passing null resource to findByResource and later dereferencing resource.getScopes() throws NPE, turning an authorization check into a 500. Same pattern in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(). Guard for null and return false.
